indicators.note: one is placed in the middle of the word for a turn, so this signals putting one piece inside another

parts.note: a turn in a game is your move
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A film critic flicks through the pages, taking one each in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside MOVE (a turn at chess). 'Flick' is informal for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A flick is slang for a film shown at the cinema.

clue.text: Pack up work, look up old traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the packing word is reversed

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: a second up, again in a down clue, reverses the looking word

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Someone packs up their work and looks out for an elderly tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'up' turns CRAM into MARC; the second turns LO into OL. 'old traveller' looks like the definition, but 'old' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant who journeyed to China and the court of Kublai Khan.

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
V, I and D are the Roman numerals for five, one and five hundred

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman statue is impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt entirely in Roman numerals: V, I, V, I, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivid colours or images are bright and arresting.

clue.text: Angered, to put it another way

definitions.text: Angered, to put it another way

indicators.note: putting the word another way rearranges its letters

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker rephrases a description of someone's temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put it another way' rearranges ANGERED, and the result means the same thing, so the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious is the same state as being made cross.

indicators.note: the rock word holds the fissure word within it, so contains signals an enclosure

parts.note: coal is a sedimentary rock
a chine is a deep narrow ravine or cleft, as on the Isle of Wight coast

explanation.surface: A geologist notes a reddish cliff with a crack running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' signals the enclosure. A chine is a steep cleft in a cliff, a word mostly used for the ravines of southern England's coast; coal counts as a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson dye made from crushed insects, so it names a shade of scarlet.

parts.note: a hippy is someone who has dropped out of conventional society

explanation.surface: A Tory dropout takes up joinery.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIPPY is British slang for a carpenter or joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a chippy is a joiner, someone who works with wood.

clue.text: May one, when one's enclosed, turn into a saint?

parts.note: can means may, is permitted to

indicators.note: being enclosed means held inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: taken as the word as written
one's is I'S, Roman one plus S

explanation.surface: Could a person be made a saint once they are shut away in a cloister?
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' signals the insertion, and 'one's' must be read as I plus S. The surface suggests an enclosed religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: To canonise is to declare officially that someone is a saint.

definitions.meaning: to tend is to be disposed or ... towards something
to bend or lean in a direction

explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed to something and leaning or sloping are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Dear old partner in a brown study

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a brown study is a state of deep thought

explanation.surface: A former lover sits lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' means costly here, not an affectionate address.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means costing a lot of money.

definitions.meaning: a lining fitted within something, as in a bin bag

explanation.definitionFit: Both an inner lining, such as for a bin, and a large passenger vessel.

clue.text: Return part of garment — one side

parts.note: revers is the turned-back lapel of a jacket or coat
I is the Roman numeral for one
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A tailor sends back part of a coat with only one side finished.
explanation.walkthrough: REVERS is a lapel turned back to show its lining. In cricket the ON side is the leg side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversion is a going back to a former state, a return to it.

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
clothes being worn are said to be on

explanation.surface: A rooster is pictured wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated male chicken fattened for the table.

clue.text: One's no longer working, having improperly ignored one lapse

indicators.note: letters used improperly are put in the wrong order, so the three words are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired worker has carelessly let one slip go unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' rearranges IGNORED ONE LAPSE, all fifteen letters. 'One's' is read as 'one who is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner of advanced years is someone retired from paid employment.

clue.text: Cleric interrupting bishop about to go too far

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other, so interrupting signals an insertion

parts.note: Odo was the Norman Bishop of Bayeux, half-brother of William the Conqueror

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the cleric's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for a reverend clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar butts in on a bishop who is about to overstep the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the cleric and 'interrupting' places him inside the bishop who commissioned the Bayeux Tapestry. 'Bishop' wants to be B; it is a named bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it to excess.

indicators.note: a broken truce falls apart, so its letters with the next word are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: No ceasefire held, and fighting resumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges TRUCE NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a clash between opposing forces.

indicators.note: a freak arrangement is an abnormal one, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer calls a rare eclipse a freak event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freak' rearranges ECLIPSE plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal synonym of special or particular, standing out from the ordinary.

clue.text: Untold millions wear the silliest materials

indicators.note: the clothes made from the shuffled letters are worn around the millions letter, so it goes inside
the silliest letters are raw materials to be made into something new, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of people dress in ridiculous fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials' rearranges SILLIEST into LIITLESS, and 'wear' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Untold means too great to be counted, without bounds.

clue.text: Rejoin a race in a straight stretch

indicators.note: the race goes in the stretch of water, signalling an insertion

parts.note: a reach is a straight stretch of river between bends
the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A runner rejoins the race on the home straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion. The TT (Tourist Trophy) motorcycle races are held on the Isle of Man; a reach is a straight stretch of river.
explanation.definitionFit: To reattach is to fasten back together, joining again.

parts.note: once means at some time in the past
someone busy over a task is engaged with it

explanation.surface: A former fiancé is now married to someone who does surveys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' tempts as ON, as in a phone line, but it goes with 'with': working over something is being engaged with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick once-over is a rapid inspection or look.

clue.text: Marsupial giving observation post a big problem

parts.note: OP is the military abbreviation for observation post
OS is outsize, a big clothing size
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An animal is causing great trouble for soldiers at a lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label.
explanation.definitionFit: The American opossum is a pouched mammal, carrying its young like a kangaroo.

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the cooking word, so into signals an insertion

parts.note: to steam food is one way to cook it

explanation.surface: A chef dashes straight into the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside STEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a small river, and to stream is to flow or run.

clue.text: Vehicle taking so-called road over the hill

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the road piece comes first
so-called means as it is called or spoken, so the road word is given by sound

parts.note: a track is a rough road
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A truck takes a track over the hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' gives TRAC by its sound, TRACK; 'over' puts it above TOR, a Dartmoor hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a farm vehicle used to pull machinery.

clue.text: Like the rim of a wheel, we hear

indicators.note: something we hear is spoken, so the wheel-rim word is given by its sound

parts.note: a felloe is the outer rim of a spoked wheel

explanation.surface: Something resembles the rim of a wheel, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is a noun here: an equal, as in 'we shall not see his like again'. It looks like a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: One's like is one's equal or counterpart, a matching companion.

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, an illegal drug
goods being sold are on the market

explanation.surface: A horse from the hills is up for auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mountain' is the definition in the sense of a glut, as in a butter mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody will buy because of a huge surplus is a glut, an unsaleable mountain of goods.

definitions.meaning: low spirits, as in being down in the mouth
squalid run-down spots, or rubbish tips

explanation.definitionFit: Low spirits, and shabby run-down spots or tips, are both senses of the plural noun.

definitions.meaning: in card games the court cards are honours
A book of the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: A Cambridge college, high court cards in bridge, and two books of the Old Testament all share the name.

parts.note: met means came across

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the quiet word is read backwards

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A shy person met some ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns SH into HS. METHS is British slang for methylated spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Meths is short for methylated spirit, denatured alcohol used as fuel.

definitions.meaning: simultaneously, everyone at the same moment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both abruptly and simultaneously, two senses of happening in one instant.

parts.note: scrim is a loosely woven cotton or linen fabric
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Cloth and a writer feature in a craft class.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw is carving or engraving on bone or ivory, a sailor's craft.

clue.text: Bloomers that were responsible for wars

definitions.meaning: the Wars of the ... were fought between the houses of York and Lancaster

explanation.definitionFit: Garden flowers that also named the fifteenth-century English civil conflict between York and Lancaster.
